query: As of July 13 2026, what is the current status of the Eastern Pacific hurricane season? Are there any active tropical storms or disturbances being monitored by NHC that could become named storm Elida (5th storm) or later? List all named EPAC storms of 2026 so far with formation dates, and any current NHC tropical weather outlook areas of interest east of 140W.
answer:
The research is complete. Summary of what I found:

**Core answer:** As of July 13, 2026, the Eastern Pacific had produced **four** named storms (Amanda, Boris, Cristina, Douglas) — all tropical-storm strength, no hurricanes — and had **zero active tropical cyclones**. Elida was indeed the next (5th) name.

**The July 13 NHC outlook** (retrieved from the Wayback Machine, plus the 5 AM and 11 AM PDT products from NHC's own refresh pages) listed two areas east of 140°W:
- **Invest EP96** offshore of southwestern Mexico, climbing 60% → 70% → 80% at 48h through the day, steady at 90% at 7 days. This became TD Five-E at 2100 UTC July 14 and **Tropical Storm Elida at 0900 UTC July 15**.
- An unformed low expected mid-week (near 0% / 60%), which became TD Six-E on July 19 → **Fausto**.

A third area (a dying low WSW of Baja) was dropped from the outlook during July 13. Two more areas — CP90 and CP91 — sat west of 140°W in CPHC territory; neither developed, and either would have taken a Central Pacific name (Lala), not Elida.

**Two things worth flagging for downstream use:**
1. TechTimes (July 12, 2026) reported the 5th name as "**Emilia**" — that's wrong; NHC's 2026 list has Elida. Any model picking up that article would be misled.
2. Elida peaked at 70 mph / 990 mb and **never became a hurricane**, despite NHC's own initial forecast calling for 85 kt and Yale Climate Connections expecting it to be the season's first hurricane.

Everything is sourced primarily to NHC operational advisories and archived outlook text rather than secondary reporting. One gap: NHC's monthly Tropical Weather Summaries for June and July 2026 are still unpublished, so no post-month authoritative basin summary exists yet.

key_facts: As of July 13, 2026, the Eastern Pacific basin (east of 140W) had produced exactly FOUR named storms: Amanda, Boris, Cristina, and Douglas. Elida is the 5th name on the 2026 EPAC list (a reuse of the 2020 list).

There were NO active tropical cyclones anywhere in the NHC/CPHC area of responsibility on July 13, 2026 — all three EPAC Tropical Weather Outlooks issued that day (5 AM, 11 AM, 5 PM PDT) lack an 'Active Systems' header. Douglas, the most recent storm, had dissipated around July 3-5.
All four storms through July 13 peaked as tropical storms; the season had produced ZERO hurricanes by that date.

NHC was monitoring two areas east of 140W on July 13, 2026 (a third was dropped during the day): Invest EP96 offshore of southwestern Mexico, and a not-yet-formed low offshore of southern/southwestern Mexico.
Invest EP96 formation probabilities rose through July 13: 60%/90% (5 AM PDT), 70%/90% (11 AM PDT, first tagged EP96), 80%/90% (5 PM PDT). By 11 AM PDT July 14 it was near 100%/near 100%.
The EP96 invest tag was applied at 17:38 UTC on July 13, 2026, per the GDACS archive of the NHC GTWO shapefile.
EP96 became Tropical Depression Five-E at 2100 UTC July 14, 2026 (14.8N 109.2W, 35 mph, 1006 mb) and was upgraded to Tropical Storm Elida at 0900 UTC July 15, 2026 (advisory 3, 40 mph, 1003 mb).
The second EPAC area of interest on July 13 ('Offshore of Southern and Southwestern Mexico', near 0%/60% all day) became Tropical Depression Six-E at 0300 UTC July 19 and then Tropical Storm Fausto.

A third EPAC area ('Central and Western East Pacific', a low WSW of Baja) was listed at 10%/10% at 5 AM PDT July 13, downgraded to near 0%/near 0% by 11 AM PDT, and removed entirely from the 5 PM PDT outlook. It never developed.

Two additional areas in the same outlook (CP91 well south of Hawaii, CP90 well southwest of Hawaii) were west of 140W and would have received CPHC names (Lala), not Elida. Neither developed; no Central Pacific cyclone formed until Lala on Aug 12-13, 2026.

Climatology: the average date for the EPAC's 5th named storm is July 23. With Elida forming July 15, the 2026 season ran about 9 days ahead of schedule on named storms — but behind climatology on hurricanes (average date for the 2nd EPAC hurricane is July 15, and 2026 had zero as of July 13).

Elida peaked at 70 mph / 990 mb at 1500 UTC July 18, 2026 (advisory 16) — it never reached hurricane strength, despite NHC's initial forecast calling for 85 kt and media reports expecting it to be the season's first hurricane.

The 2026 season's first hurricane was Fausto (July 20 or July 22 — Wikipedia sections disagree). Genevieve became the first major and first Category 5 hurricane, peaking at 160 mph / 925 mb after forming July 24.

MEDIA ERROR TO NOTE: TechTimes (July 12, 2026) incorrectly reported the 5th named storm would be called 'Emilia'. The NHC 2026 Eastern North Pacific list has Elida in the fifth slot; 'Emilia' is not on the list.

NOAA's May 21, 2026 seasonal outlook called for an above-normal EPAC season: 15-22 named storms, 9-14 hurricanes, 5-9 major hurricanes, citing a developing El Nino. Mexico's SMN (April 22, 2026) forecast 18-21 named storms, 9-11 hurricanes, 4-5 major hurricanes.

As of the current outlook (5 AM PDT Aug 19, 2026), the EPAC/CPAC has Hurricane Lala active, plus EP90 at 70%/80% and an area south-southwest of Mexico at near 0%/80%. Season ACE stands at approximately 66.8 units.
